home.title: Compressor
home.lead: A real machine, with a history of real data, served by a backend of its own. It is the second module of the demo and the only one that does not read this plant’s ICONICS server.

service.title: Service status
service.sub: The only thing this module can check on its own today
service.down: The prediction backend does not respond
service.ownMachine: Its own machine, separate from the ICONICS server and from the AI one

limits.title: Limitations
limits.sub: What has to be said out loud before showing any curve from this module
items: The data does NOT come from ICONICS: another backend serves it, on another machine. Nothing seen here can be cross-referenced with the tank or with the vibration system.
The history is fed from a spreadsheet whose exact contents are not yet inventoried: we do not know which variables it has, nor in what unit.
There is no live reading of this machine. Everything queried is the past.
The predictive model has no published validated error yet, so no projection can be quoted as reliable.

pending.stillNeeds: What is missing to build it
pending.noFakeData: This screen deliberately draws no sample data: an invented curve on a plant dashboard reads as a measurement.

historico.resumen: How a variable moved between two dates, with its dated extremes — not the replay of an event, but the free query.
mostrara: The curve of a variable over the requested period
Minimum and maximum, with the exact time they occurred
Stretches with no sample, declared as gaps and not drawn as zero
Comparison of the same variable between two periods
necesita: A free-series endpoint: which parameters it accepts and what format each sample has
The maximum window it allows, and whether it paginates
What it returns for a stretch with no data — it must be distinguishable from a real zero
How it signals a service failure, so it is never narrated as absence of data

correlacion.resumen: Whether two or more compressor variables moved together over the same window, with their coefficient and its reading in plain words.
mostrara: The coefficient of each pair, from −1 to 1, and what it means in plain language
The window it was measured over, and how many samples support it
A warning when the window is too short to claim anything
necesita: Deciding who computes it: the API, or us over the series (Monitoring already has that code)
If the API computes it: which coefficient it uses and over what resampling
The free-series endpoint, if the computation happens on this side

pronostico.resumen: How a compressor variable will behave over the coming days — always with its uncertainty alongside, never as a line on its own.
mostrara: The projection of a variable to the requested horizon
Its margin of error, with the same visual weight as the curve itself
The model’s validated error, stated on the screen and not hidden
An explicit refusal when the requested horizon exceeds what the model supports
necesita: The forecast endpoint: which horizon it allows and what it returns per sample
The model’s validated error, published — without it no projection can be quoted
Which confidence interval it delivers, if any

variables.resumen: What this machine measures, in what unit and over what range — the equivalent of the signal catalogue the plant machines already have.
mostrara: Each variable with its readable name, its unit and its valid range
Which ones have a historical series and which only a loose value
From what date there is data, and whether the history is contiguous
What canNOT be claimed about each one, just as the two plant systems do
necesita: The inventory of the history: exactly which columns the spreadsheet feeding the API brings
The unit of each variable — without it, a number on screen means nothing
An endpoint listing the variables, or the list agreed in writing
